attributes.title: Inspection gaps
attributes.description: Traffic that left with part of it uninspected: inspection did not finish under a fail-open policy, or an attachment could not be read - an image, an encrypted document, something over the size limit. Should be zero; a non-zero value invalidates the other panels for that period rather than merely being untidy.
attributes.visState: {"title": "Inspection gaps", "type": "metric", "aggs": [{"id": "1", "enabled": true, "type": "count", "schema": "metric", "params": {}}], "params": {"addTooltip": true, "addLegend": false, "type": "metric", "metric": {"percentageMode": false, "useRanges": false, "colorSchema": "Green to Red", "metricColorMode": "None", "colorsRange": [{"from": 0, "to": 10000}], "labels": {"show": true}, "invertColors": false, "style": {"bgFill": "#000", "bgColor": false, "labelColor": false, "subText": "", "fontSize": 36}}}}

attributes.title: High-value identifiers inside documents
attributes.description: PESEL, IBAN or a payment card found inside an attachment rather than typed into the prompt. A document may hold one row of many people's data, so this is a different incident from someone pasting their own number, and it cannot be masked - a PDF cannot be rewritten without corrupting it.

attributes.title: Repeat offenders
attributes.description: Workstations that tripped the repetition rules. One paste is an accident; eight in five minutes is a habit, and only this panel tells them apart.

attributes.title: Typed, or attached
attributes.description: Where the identifier was. Someone typing a PESEL is one person's slip; someone attaching a contract containing one may be sending a file full of other people's data. Without this field the two are the same row.
attributes.visState: {"title": "Typed, or attached", "type": "pie", "aggs": [{"id": "1", "enabled": true, "type": "count", "schema": "metric", "params": {}}, {"id": "2", "enabled": true, "type": "terms", "schema": "segment", "params": {"field": "data.source", "orderBy": "1", "order": "desc", "size": 4, "otherBucket": false, "otherBucketLabel": "other", "missingBucket": false, "missingBucketLabel": "missing"}}], "params": {"type": "pie", "addTooltip": true, "addLegend": true, "legendPosition": "right", "isDonut": true, "labels": {"show": true, "values": true, "truncate": 100}}}

attributes.title: What kind of file
attributes.description: PDF, Office document, plain text - or opaque, which means it could not be read at all: an image, an archive, something encrypted. An opaque slice that keeps growing is a coverage gap, not a quiet period.
attributes.visState: {"title": "What kind of file", "type": "pie", "aggs": [{"id": "1", "enabled": true, "type": "count", "schema": "metric", "params": {}}, {"id": "2", "enabled": true, "type": "terms", "schema": "segment", "params": {"field": "data.attachment_kind", "orderBy": "1", "order": "desc", "size": 6, "otherBucket": false, "otherBucketLabel": "other", "missingBucket": false, "missingBucketLabel": "missing"}}], "params": {"type": "pie", "addTooltip": true, "addLegend": true, "legendPosition": "right", "isDonut": true, "labels": {"show": true, "values": true, "truncate": 100}}}

attributes.title: What the gateway did
attributes.description: Blocked, masked, advised or observed. The advisory-first design means most traffic should be masked or advised; a wall of blocks means the policy is miscalibrated.

attributes.title: Which files keep coming back
attributes.description: One row per document, identified by the digest of its bytes rather than by a name - a filename would carry the very data this trail exists to keep out, and it changes the moment somebody retries a refused upload. A digest does not. The same value appearing under two workstations, or after a block, is an abuse path rather than an accident. It equals sha256sum of the file, so a document you already hold can be looked up here.
